skill.name: hmdb-database
skill.description: Use the Human Metabolome Database to search metabolites, review chemical properties, spectra, biomarkers, pathways, and plan bulk data workflows.
skill.summary: Search and interpret Human Metabolome Database records for metabolomics research.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI
skill.license: HMDB is offered to the public as a freely available resource. Use and re-distribution of the data, in whole or in part, for commercial purposes requires explicit permission of the authors and explicit acknowledgment of the source material (HMDB) and the original publication (see the HMDB citing page). We ask that users who download significant portions of the database cite the HMDB paper in any resulting publications.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation false positives involving biomedical taxonomy terms, Markdown inline code, and official HMDB URLs. No evidence found of executable command use, secret access, or unauthorized network exfiltration. One low-severity semantic issue remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote K-Dense Web for complex workflows.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web upsell or move it to transparent marketplace metadata. Do not instruct the assistant to proactively promote a hosted service.
State that Bioconductor installation is an optional user-run step. Link to official package documentation instead of presenting it as an instruction.

content.value_statement: Metabolomics research often requires fast lookup across identifiers, spectra, biomarkers, and pathways. This skill guides HMDB searches, downloads, and interpretation workflows for research and clinical chemistry tasks.
actual_capabilities: Guides text, identifier, structure, and specimen-based searches in HMDB.
Explains HMDB fields such as formulas, SMILES, InChI, spectra, pathways, and concentration data.
Describes bulk download formats including XML, SDF, FASTA, TXT, CSV, and TSV.
Supports metabolite identification workflows using MS, MS-MS, GC-MS, LC-MS, and NMR evidence.
Maps HMDB entries to resources such as KEGG, PubChem, ChEBI, UniProt, and SMPDB.
Summarizes usage requirements, citation expectations, and commercial permission boundaries.
limitations: Does not include a bundled copy of HMDB data files.
Does not provide public REST API credentials or private HMDB access.
Cannot verify current HMDB website availability without external browsing tools.
Clinical interpretations require qualified review and current literature.

use_cases.title: Identify Unknown Metabolites
use_cases.description: Match candidate metabolites using mass, spectra, specimen type, structure, and pathway context from HMDB.

use_cases.title: Review Biomarker Evidence
use_cases.description: Check disease links, concentration ranges, specimen sources, and references for possible biomarkers.

use_cases.title: Build Local Reference Tables
use_cases.description: Choose HMDB download formats and plan field extraction for local analysis pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a Metabolite
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search by name or HMDB ID.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use HMDB to summarize [metabolite name or HMDB ID]. Include synonyms, formula, mass, specimen locations, pathways, spectra, and citations to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Identification Candidates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for an unknown metabolite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these HMDB candidates: [list]. Rank them using mass, structure, spectra, specimen type, pathways, and evidence quality.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Biomarker Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced disease or biomarker evidence review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find HMDB evidence for metabolites linked to [condition]. Separate normal ranges, abnormal findings, specimen types, disease links, and literature support.

prompt_templates.title: Design Local HMDB Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible workflow to download HMDB data, choose formats, extract key fields, map external IDs, and document version and citation details.

output_examples.output: A concise metabolite profile with names, formula, mass, specimen locations, spectra availability, pathway links, and citations to verify.

output_examples.input: Compare three candidate metabolites for an unknown LC-MS peak.
output_examples.output: A ranked comparison that weighs mass match, spectra evidence, specimen plausibility, pathway context, and follow-up validation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan an HMDB download workflow for a local metabolomics database.
output_examples.output: A workflow covering format choice, required fields, external ID mapping, version tracking, citation notes, and permission checks.

best_practices: Verify identifications with at least two evidence types, such as spectra and mass.
Record HMDB version, accession IDs, and citation details in research outputs.
Use downloaded datasets for large analyses instead of repeated manual website queries.
anti_patterns: Treating predicted spectra or concentrations as confirmed experimental evidence.
Using HMDB data commercially without checking permission requirements.
Relying on a name match alone for metabolite identification.

faq.question: Does this skill include the HMDB data files?
faq.answer: No. It explains how to search, download, and interpret HMDB data. You still need access to HMDB resources.

faq.question: Can it use a public HMDB REST API?
faq.answer: HMDB does not provide a public REST API. Programmatic access may require downloaded files or direct HMDB team contact.

faq.question: Is it suitable for clinical diagnosis?
faq.answer: No. It can organize HMDB evidence, but clinical decisions require qualified review and current clinical context.

faq.question: Can it help identify metabolites from spectra?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines MS, MS-MS, GC-MS, LC-MS, and NMR evidence checks for candidate identification.

faq.question: What data formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers XML, SDF, FASTA, TXT, CSV, and TSV formats described by HMDB.

faq.question: What citations are needed?
faq.answer: Record HMDB accession IDs, database version, download date, and the HMDB publication required by the data license.
